title: "Uploading a Presentation Video to YouTube: Titles, Descriptions and Chapters" (blog explainer)

brief.story: A clear explainer of the post.

slides.title: Uploading a Presentation Video to YouTube
bullets: The video is only half the job
slides.notes: Your video is only half the job on YouTube. The title, description, chapters and thumbnail decide whether anyone finds it, and whether they stay.

slides.title: Prepare the file before you upload
bullets: Watch it once, all the way through
Check typos, audio and internal information
slides.notes: Before uploading, export an MP4 and watch it all the way through. Catch typos and internal information, and jot down when each new section starts.

slides.title: Write a title people search for
bullets: Stronger: How to Plan a Q4 Marketing Budget for a Small Business
No all caps or vague teasers
slides.notes: A good title says what viewers will learn, in the words they'd type. So Q4 Webinar becomes How to Plan a Q4 Marketing Budget for a Small Business.

slides.title: Structure a useful description
bullets: First two lines: a plain summary
What you'll learn: three to five bullets
slides.notes: Make the first two lines a plain summary, since they show before the more link. Then add three to five bullets, your chapters and your links.

slides.title: Build chapters from your slides
bullets: One timestamp and title per line
slides.notes: List timestamps starting at zero, one per line with a title. Your section divider slides and point-making headlines become ready-made chapter titles.

slides.title: Make the video first
slides.notes: Your slide headlines and speaker notes give you the chapters and description. On Pro, a.i. directs your deck into a video that holds viewers. Try Basic first at powerpoint2vid.com.
